content.title: About
content.content: Snowpeas are young pea pods harvested at the earliest stage of growth. The NS (non‑shelled) version refers to whole, intact pods, and “form” indicates that the pods retain their natural shape. The product is ready to eat after cooking: it keeps a crisp texture, a delicate sweet flavor, and a bright green color.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Snowpeas belong to the legume family and are close relatives of garden peas and beans.
Pods are picked when they are only 3–5 cm long, which makes them especially tender and sweet.
The NS (non‑shelled) variant is popular in gourmet cuisine for its visual appeal.
Snowpeas are rich in B‑vitamins, vitamin C, and folate.
In Japan they are often served as salads or side dishes with sushi.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Snowpeas provide about 5 g of protein per 100 g, making them a good protein source for vegetarians.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many legumes, snowpeas contain virtually no fat, suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The pods contain vitamin C, vitamin K, folate, iron, and magnesium, which support immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Snowpeas raise blood sugar slowly, which is beneficial for people with pre‑diabetes.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to legumes, including snowpeas.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Like other legumes, snowpeas can cause flatulence in sensitive people.

items.title: Requires cooking
items.content: Raw pods contain anti‑nutritional factors and should be cooked before consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook snowpeas in boiling water for 3–5 minutes until tender, then shock in ice water to preserve the bright color. They can be added to salads, soups, stews, used as a side for fish or meat, or incorporated into Asian dishes such as stir‑fries or sushi rolls.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked snowpeas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. Raw pods are best kept in a cool, dry place in a ventilated bag, where they stay fresh for about 7 days.
